Start

Who the agent is, and the sign-in for people without a token.

whoami reads

Who you work for (email, roles), how this server is signed in (an AI connection's token with its name, a session, or not yet), whether the editor's tools are open, the API and the editor app whose links every result hands back.

whoami {}
Details

Call it first.

sign_in_request writes

Starts a sign-in by e-mail, for people without a token.

sign_in_request { email }
ParameterTypeWhat
emailstring
Details

the API mails a 6-digit code to the address (locally with MAIL_TRANSPORT=log it lands in the mail log). Ask the person for the code, then sign_in_verify. Not needed when OSCT_EDITOR_TOKEN is set (a token made on the editor's experiences page, AI connections).

sign_in_verify writes

Finishes the sign-in with the code from the mail.

sign_in_verify { requestId, code }
ParameterTypeWhat
requestIdstring
codestringthe 6-digit code
Details

the session token is kept for this process (never shown). With the role editor the editor's tools open.

describe_content_model reads

What you may write.

describe_content_model { experience? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experience optionalstringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

node types (and node names), placement (units, defaults), filters, components with their parameters, post-processing passes, the environment, scenes and surfaces (with their place), entries (scene, surface), a target's place, entry categories, scene presets – from the shared content contract. With experience: also the compiled plugins its configuration declares with the components, layers, node types and passes they recorded (their parameters), and the Code tab's sources with the types read from them.

Reading

Nothing here changes anything.

list_experiences reads

The instance's experiences.

list_experiences {}
Details

id, title, author, the scene it opens on (initialScene), number of scenes, content schema, last publish, live (the environments serving a build of it – every experience has its own store in each; empty: draft only) – and the editor's link of each; environments = the environments whose content store could not be read (where an experience is live there is unknown).

get_experience reads

An experience's tree (content schema 3.0).

get_experience { experience }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

the experience, its scenes in order (id, label, group, surfaces with their size and place, passes) each with its entries (id, title, category, scene, surface) and each entry's target (id, imageSrc, place, entity inline or { ref }), and the groups. Shared entities: get_entity; one scene with every entity resolved: get_scene.

list_scenes reads

The experience's scenes in order (a scene is one step of the experience – a double page, a cover, a wall, a room).

list_scenes { experience }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

id, position, label, group, passes, its surfaces (id, label, widthMm, heightMm, place in the scene, reference – the editor-only reference image, null: none), how many entries and targets lie on it – and the groups with their scenes.

get_scene reads

One scene (its label, group, surfaces with size and place, passes) with its entries and targets, every target's entity resolved.

get_scene { experience, scene }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenestringthe scene's id (get_experience, list_scenes)
Details

an inline entity as it is, a shared one as the entity under entity with its ref next to it (put_entity changes the shared entity for every target using it; put_target with entity gives the target its own). Surface reference images: list_scenes.

get_entries reads

Every entry of the experience in the experience's order with its fields as written – title, category, scene, surface, body (Markdown with the experience's variables), author, image, caption (the line under the picture), media (a link's URL)

get_entries { experience, category?, search? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
category optional"glossary" | "video" | "text" | "link"
search optionalstringa word the title, body or tags hold (case does not matter)
Details

, tags – and its target's id and image (null: read in the list only). Optionally only one category, or the entries whose title, body or tags hold a word.

get_entity reads

One shared entity of the experience by its ref (EntityData, the node tree); the refs are in get_experience's targets ({ ref }).

get_entity { experience, ref }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
refstring

get_draft reads

The experience's draft as the content version the engine loads.

get_draft { experience, part }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
part"manifest" | "configuration" | "files"
Details

manifest (build, hash), configuration (the whole game configuration, content schema 3.0, assembled from the rows now) or files (its files.json). Large – prefer get_scene for one scene.

Scenes, surfaces and groups

add_scene writes

Adds a scene anywhere in the order, to any experience.

add_scene { experience, preset?, after?, before?, position?, id?, label?, group?, surfaces? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
preset optional"double" | "single" | "wall"
after optionalstringafter this scene (list_scenes)
before optionalstringbefore this scene
position optionalintegerat this index (0 = first)
id optionalstring
label optionalstringwhat the reader shows for the scene – free text
group optionalstringa group of the experience (list_scenes)
surfaces optional{ id, label, widthMm, heightMm, place }[]instead of the preset's
Details

preset (default double) – double, single, wall: double = one surface 460 × 320 mm (a double page), single = one page 230 × 320 mm (a cover is a single scene first in the order), wall = 2000 × 1500 mm standing ahead (rx 90) – gives its surfaces unless surfaces names them (surfaces without a place are laid in a row). Place it with after / before (a scene id) or position (an index); none = last. Optional: id (made by the server unless given), label (what the reader's switcher shows – 186–187, Studio wall), group. The change is recorded.

put_scene writes

Changes a scene.

put_scene { experience, scene, label?, group?, surfaces?, passes?, logic?, apply? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenestringthe scene's id (list_scenes)
label optionalstring
group optionalstring | null
surfaces optional{ id, label, widthMm, heightMm, place }[]
passes optional{ type, enabled }[] | null
logic optionalobject | nullthe scene's rules { rules: [{ on, when?, do }], canvas? } (content schema 5.0, describe_content_model logic); null removes them
apply optionalbooleanlet surfaces go that entries or targets lie on – only after the person's yes
Details

label (free text – what the reader's switcher shows), group (a group of the experience; null takes it out – the scene stays in place), surfaces (the whole list, at least one – add, remove, resize, label, place: { id, label?, widthMm, heightMm, place? }; a surface without a place is laid in a row; a surface that goes takes its reference image), passes = the scene's own post-processing that replaces the experience's here ([{ type, enabled?, …parameters }] – the built-in types and the passes of the experience's plugins, describe_content_model { experience } passes; [] turns post-processing off here, null gives the scene the experience's passes again), logic = the scene's rules (content schema 5.0: { rules: [{ on, when?, do }], canvas? } – live while the scene is open, they listen to the bus and name nodes by address target:<targetId>/<node name>; describe_content_model logic; null removes them). Send what changes; checked against the contract. Surfaces that entries or targets lie on go only with apply: true – the first call answers 409 surfaces-in-use naming them (details.entries, details.targets): show the person; with their yes call again with apply: true – the entries stay on the scene without a surface, the targets lose their place (cleared). A change is recorded.

put_surface writes

Changes ONE surface of a scene without sending the whole list (put_scene sends the whole list).

put_surface { experience, scene, surface, remove?, label?, preset?, widthMm?, heightMm?, place?, position?, apply? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenestringthe scene's id (list_scenes)
surfacestringthe surface's id – one the scene does not have adds a surface
remove optionalbooleantrue removes the surface (nothing else may be sent with it)
label optionalstring | nullwhat is printed on it (186–187, Cover); null or empty: none
preset optional"double" | "single" | "wall"its size from a format: double page, single page, wall
widthMm optionalnumberits width in mm (wins over the preset's)
heightMm optionalnumberits height in mm (wins over the preset's)
place optional{ x, y, z, rx, ry, rz }where the surface lies in the scene's coordinate system – its centre x, y, z in mm, rx, ry, rz in degrees (Euler XYZ, default 0); origin on the table at the middle of the first row (a double page: its spine), +x right, +y up, +z towards the reader; unrotated it lies flat face up, its top edge away from the reader – a wall ahead stands up: rx 90. Left out: the server lays every surface without one in a row
position optionalintegerits index in the scene's surfaces (0 = first)
apply optionalbooleanlet a surface go that entries or targets lie on – only after the person's yes
Details

surface by id – an id the scene does not have **adds** it (its size from preset – double 460 × 320, single 230 × 320, wall 2000 × 1500 mm – or widthMm and heightMm; without a place the server lays it in a row), a known one **changes** the fields sent (label – null: none –, preset or widthMm / heightMm for its size, place), position **moves** it to that index (0 = first), remove: true **removes** it (never the scene's last). Targets keep their place in mm when a surface gets smaller – check them with get_scene / render_scene. A surface that entries or targets lie on goes only with apply: true: the first call answers 409 surfaces-in-use naming them – show the person; with their yes call again with apply: true. Reads the scene's list (list_scenes), writes it with the one change (PUT …/scenes/{id}); a change is recorded.

set_surface_reference writes

Sets, replaces or removes a surface's reference image – the picture the editor's stage shows on that surface (a scanned double page, a photo of the wall).

set_surface_reference { experience, scene, surface, url?, fit?, name? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenestringthe scene's id (list_scenes)
surfacestringthe surface's id in that scene (list_scenes)
url optionalstring | nulla Library image's URL; null removes the reference
fit optional"cover" | "contain" | "stretch"
name optionalstring
Details

Editor-only: never in the content, readers never see it. url: an image of the experience's Library (list_assets – upload_asset first, best with fit: "reference", scene and surface) or an imported file's /assets/content/… path; null removes it. fit: cover (default – cut to cover the surface), contain (fit inside) or stretch; a replace keeps the fit it had. name defaults to the Library's. fit / name without url change the present one. list_scenes shows each surface's reference. A change is recorded (revertable).

move_scenes writes

Moves one or several scenes as a block (in their present order) – after / before a scene or to a position (an index among the scenes that stay) – or into a group (group.

move_scenes { experience, scenes, after?, before?, position?, group?, apply? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenesstring[]the scenes to move (list_scenes)
after optionalstringafter this scene (list_scenes)
before optionalstringbefore this scene
position optionalintegerat this index (0 = first)
group optionalstring | nulla group to move them into, or null to take them out of theirs
apply optionalbooleanthe second step: write the plan the person agreed to
Details

after its last scene unless a place is given) or out of their group (group: null: they stay in place, unless they sit inside it – then right after it). **Two steps**: without apply nothing is written – the plan answers the new order, the scenes that moved and the groups changes. Show it to the person; with their yes call again with the same arguments and apply: true. Every change is recorded.

delete_scene replaces or removes

Removes a scene with everything on it – its entries, their targets, the entities used only there and, only if asked, the Library files used only there – in **two steps**.

delete_scene { experience, scene, confirm?, deleteFiles? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenestringthe scene's id (list_scenes)
confirm optionalstringthe second step: the confirmation id of the impact the person agreed to
deleteFiles optionalbooleanwith confirm: also delete the Library files used only here – only when the person asked for it
Details

the first call removes nothing and answers impact (the scene, the entries, targets and entities that go, the shared entities that are kept with their other targets, the Library files used only here and used elsewhere) and a short-lived confirmation. Show the impact to the person and ask; only with their yes call again with the same arguments and confirm: <confirmation.id>. deleteFiles: true also deletes the files used only here – only when the person asked for it (off by default; files used elsewhere are never deleted). 409 initial-scene for the scene the experience opens on. Every removed row is in the change log, naming this AI connection.

group_scenes writes

Makes a group of the picked scenes – a label over several scenes (Front matter, a chapter, a room).

group_scenes { experience, label, scenes, id?, apply? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
labelstring
scenesstring[]
id optionalstring
apply optionalboolean
Details

one stop of the reader's bottom switcher. The scenes come together where the first of them is (in their present order; a scene of another group leaves it). **Two steps**: without apply the plan (the group's id and label, the new order, what moves); with the person's yes the same call with apply: true. The id: id, else made from the label. Rename with rename_group, ungroup with ungroup.

rename_group writes

Renames a group of the experience (list_scenes groups).

rename_group { experience, group, label }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
groupstring
labelstring
Details

A change is recorded.

ungroup writes

Ungroups.

ungroup { experience, group }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
groupstring
Details

the group goes, its scenes stay where they are, in order, without a group. Nothing else changes; a change is recorded per scene and for the groups.

Targets and AR content

add_entry writes

Makes a new entry on a scene.

add_entry { experience, title, scene, surface?, category?, body?, caption?, id?, target? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
titlestring
scenestringthe entry's scene (list_scenes)
surface optionalstringone of the scene's surfaces – needed when it has several
category optional"glossary" | "video" | "text" | "link"
body optionalstring
caption optionalstringthe line under the entry's picture ("Image: … by …"), plain text
id optionalstring
target optional{ id, imageSrc, place, entity, enabled }none: an entry read only in the list
Details

scene (a scene id – list_scenes, get_experience) and surface (one of its surfaces – needed when the scene has several). Then: title, category (default glossary – the reader lists it as "Marginalia"), body (Markdown with the experience's variables – describe_content_model entryText), caption (the line under the entry's picture, plain text), and its target – imageSrc (the printed image: an uploaded image asset's url), place (where it lies on a surface of the scene, in mm), entity (its AR content as a node tree, or { ref }) – or no target: an entry read only in the list (a glossary term, a text). The id comes from the title unless given; 409 duplicate-id. The reader tracks a target after a publish.

put_target writes

Changes a target.

put_target { experience, target, entity?, ref?, imageSrc?, place?, enabled?, recognitionOff? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
targetstringthe target's id (get_scene)
entity optionalobject | null
ref optionalstringa shared entity's ref
imageSrc optionalstring
place optional{ surface, x, y, width, height } | null
enabled optionalbooleanfalse = switched off: not in the reader's experience; true = in the experience again
recognitionOff optionalbooleantrue = always the printed image, never its recognition frame made ahead; false = the experience's recognition setting decides
Details

entity = its own AR content (EntityData; null removes it), ref = a shared entity instead, imageSrc = the printed image (an uploaded image asset's url – upload it with upload_asset fit: "target", at most 1200 px), place = where it lies: { surface?, x, y, width, height? } in mm from the top left corner of a surface of its entry's scene (surface by id – required when the scene has several; null removes the place), enabled = in the reader's experience (false switches it off: the reader leaves the target and its entry out, the editor keeps both – content schema 2.26), recognitionOff = true keeps this target on its printed image even when the experience's recognition is "prepared" (content schema 4.2; false: the experience decides). Send what changes. Checked against the contract; a change is recorded.

put_entity writes

Saves (or adds) a shared entity under ref – the whole node tree (EntityData.

put_entity { experience, ref, entity }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
refstringthe shared entity's ref
entityobjectEntityData – the node tree (describe_content_model)
Details

type, assets, params, filters, components, children, text, color; describe_content_model). Checked against the content contract before it is sent; the API records a change. Every target with { ref } shows it.

Texts

update_entry writes

Changes an entry's fields – send only what changes.

update_entry { experience, entry, title?, category?, scene?, surface?, body?, author?, tags?, image?, imageLevels?, caption?, media? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
entrystringthe entry's id (get_entries, get_experience)
title optionalstring
category optional"glossary" | "video" | "text" | "link"
scene optionalstringthe scene to move it to (list_scenes)
surface optionalstring | nullone of its scene's surfaces; null: none
body optionalstring
author optionalstring | null
tags optionalstring[]
image optionalstring | nulla Library picture's url (list_assets kind image); null removes it
imageLevels optional{ level, src }[] | nullthe picture in several sizes (content schema 4.3, #331): [{ level, src }], level 512 / 1024 / 2048 (px, longest side), each a Library picture; null removes them
caption optionalstring | nullthe line under the picture, plain text; null removes it
media optionalstring | nullan http(s) URL; null removes it
Details

title, category, scene (moves it to that scene – list_scenes), surface (one of its scene's surfaces; null: none – a scene with several surfaces needs one), body (Markdown: paragraphs at blank lines, *emphasis*, **strong**, [links](https://…); the experience's variables in braces – {hasKey}, {hasKey: …|…} – describe_content_model entryText), author, tags (the whole list), image (a picture of the experience's Library: an uploaded image's url or a file of the import), caption (the line under the picture, plain text – "Image: … by …"; not the Library's credit line, set_asset_credits), media (a link's http(s) URL), imageLevels (the picture at several sizes – the reader's media quality chooses one); null removes author, image, imageLevels, caption or media. A body whose braces do not parse is refused before it is sent. The change is recorded; the person checks it in the editor.

delete_entry replaces or removes

Removes an entry with its target, the entity used only there and – only if asked – the Library files used only there, in **two steps**.

delete_entry { experience, entry, confirm?, deleteFiles? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
entrystring
confirm optionalstringthe second step: the confirmation id of the impact the person agreed to
deleteFiles optionalbooleanwith confirm: also delete the Library files used only here – only when the person asked for it
Details

the first call removes nothing and answers impact (the target, the entity that goes, a shared entity that is kept with its other targets, the Library files used only here and used elsewhere) and a short-lived confirmation. Show the impact to the person and ask; only with their yes call again with the same arguments and confirm: <confirmation.id>. deleteFiles: true also deletes the files used only here – only when the person asked for it (off by default; files used elsewhere are never deleted). Every removed row is in the change log, naming this AI connection.

update_experience writes

Changes the experience's title – the reader's splash, home page and account show it – or its printed book.

update_experience { experience, title?, book?, recognition? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
title optionalstring
book optional{ author, publisher } | nullthe printed book: { author?, publisher? } – the fields that change; null removes the printed book
recognition optional"original" | "prepared" | null"original" (default) or "prepared"; null = the default
Details

book { author, publisher? } is the printed book this experience accompanies (the splash shows the author and the publisher above Start; the onboarding itself is the app's, not the experience's). Send what changes: book { author } or { publisher } changes those fields (publisher null or "" removes it); book: null removes the printed book – an experience without one (a wall, a room, an exhibition) – only with the person's yes; a new printed book needs author. recognition (content schema 4.2) = how the reader gets its targets' recognition data: "original" (the default – made from each printed image on the phone, the path tested with every target) or "prepared" (a target's grey frame made ahead where it has one – only after a test run on the phones, with the person's yes); null = the default. The change is recorded.

Look

put_experience_passes writes

Sets the experience's post-processing – the master chain every scene without its own passes shows.

put_experience_passes { experience, passes }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
passes{ type, enabled }[] | null
Details

[{ type, enabled?, …parameters }] run in order over the rendered image (built-in types bloom, vignette, grade, and the passes the experience's plugins register – describe_content_model { experience } passes); enabled: false switches one pass off, keeping its place and values; [] = none; null removes it. A scene's own passes (put_scene) still replace it there. Checked against the contract; a change is recorded.

put_experience_appearance writes

How the experience's AR entities appear and disappear – a look per moment.

put_experience_appearance { experience, appearance }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
appearance{ reveal, found, lost } | null
Details

{ reveal?, found?, lost? }, each { type, …parameters } like a pass. reveal = the first find of a target, found = every later find, lost = the target is lost (played rewound in the look's outDuration). A moment left out takes found's look, then the default; null (or {}) removes the field – the default look plays everywhere. The whole appearance is replaced: send every moment that keeps a look. Types: the built-in inflateDissolve, printLift, fade and the looks the experience's plugins register (describe_content_model { experience } appearance, with every parameter's range and default). Checked against the contract; a change is recorded.

put_environment writes

Sets the experience's environment – the world around the reader while scanning and the onion sky.

put_environment { experience, environment }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
environment{ world, onionSky, worldSrc, skySrc } | null
Details

{ world, onionSky, worldSrc?, skySrc? } – worldSrc a glTF model (an uploaded asset's url: .glb / .gltf) in place of the built-in world's scenery, skySrc an equirectangular image (.jpg / .png / .webp) for the sky; null removes it (the default world, the onion sky on). Experience-level; the reader's Graphics switches still apply on top. Checked against the contract; a change is recorded.

Files

list_assets reads

The experience's files.

list_assets { experience, kind? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
kind optional"glb" | "gltf" | "video" | "image" | "audio" | "shader" | "subtitles"
Details

id, name, kind (glb | gltf | video | image | audio | shader | subtitles), mime, size, width / height (pixels, images and videos), durationMs (videos), version, url (what nodes and targets name – and what a plugin loads a shader by, api.loadText(url)), usages (a shader's: the plugin sources that name its url), credits (the picture credits line, null: none yet – set_asset_credits). width / height / durationMs are read from the file on upload – null when unknown (an imported file, an older upload). A video plane is one target width wide and as high as the file's proportions; scale a portrait video's node by width / height to keep it within the target's width, and time an animation by durationMs. imported: a file of the content import (no upload) – read-only.

upload_asset writes

Uploads a file from this computer into the experience's library.

upload_asset { experience, file, name?, fit?, entry?, scene?, surface? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
filestringa local file path
name optionalstringthe file name to store (default: the path's base name; a converted image ends in .webp)
fit optional"reference" | "entryImage" | "target" | "texture" | "default"an image's use: target (1200 px), reference (a surface's reference image, 2048 px), entryImage, default (2048 px)
entry optionalstringwith fit target / entryImage: the entry whose image it is – names the file <entry>_target / <entry>_image
scene optionalstringwith fit reference and surface: the scene whose surface the image is for – names the file <scene>_<surface>
surface optionalstringwith fit reference and scene: the surface (list_scenes)
Details

models (glb, gltf), videos (mp4, webm, mov), images (jpg, png, webp), sounds (mp3, m4a, ogg, wav), at most 64 MB, and shaders (glsl, frag, vert, wgsl – UTF-8 text, at most 256 KB; a plugin loads one by its url with api.loadText) and a video's subtitles (vtt – WebVTT text, at most 256 KB; named <video name>.<language>.vtt, e.g. speak.en.vtt for speak.mp4, it belongs to every video of that name in the experience and shows as its subtitle line – no node names it). Answers the asset with its url – put it into a node's assets[].src or a target's imageSrc – and the file's width / height (images, videos) and durationMs (videos), null when the file does not tell. The same bytes twice are one asset, named as the last upload names it. A script (.ts, .js) is no asset: upload_plugin. **Images go under the image rule** (#298): the API stores a jpg / png / webp as WebP (quality 82, lossless when it has transparency), upright by its EXIF orientation, metadata dropped, its longest side at most 2048 px – never scaled up – and named <name>.webp (converted says so; an instance without GD stores it as it came). Pass fit: "target" for a target's printed image (at most 1200 px). TIFF and PDF are no Library files: convert them locally first. **Named by its use** (#298) when you say it: entry with fit target / entryImage → <entry>_target.webp / <entry>_image.webp, scene + surface with fit reference (a surface's reference image, set it with set_surface_reference) → <scene>_<surface>.webp (400 invalid-use for no surface of the experience).

rename_asset writes

Renames one file of the Library by hand (#330) – an uploaded or an imported one, by its id (list_assets.

rename_asset { experience, asset, name }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
assetstringthe file's id (list_assets)
namestring
Details

a uuid, or import-…). The name only: the URL and every use stay, so nothing breaks. White space is folded; no slash, backslash or control character; the stored file's extension stays (added when the name lacks it: castle → castle.glb); at most 255 characters (400 invalid-name otherwise). For naming every used file by where it is used, plan_asset_names is the way. Names are no content: nothing to publish, no change in the experience's log.

delete_asset replaces or removes

Deletes an uploaded file (every version).

delete_asset { experience, asset, force? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
assetstringthe asset's id (list_assets)
force optionalboolean
Details

Refused while the file is used – a target, entry, entity, scene, a surface's reference image, the experience (its environment or another setting) or a plugin source names it, the same uses list_assets counts (409 asset-in-use with the usages) unless force.

set_asset_credits writes

Sets the picture credits of the experience's files (#277).

set_asset_credits { experience, items }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
items{ url, credits }[]
Details

one free text line per file, by its url (list_assets – uploaded and imported files alike), as the book prints its credits – e.g. "Book Golem by TER-JAN / DeviantArt", "Lindsey Carr, An Issue of Control, 2013. Available via DogStreets", "Gene Kelly dancing, 1944. Gjon Mili The LIFE Picture Collection/Shutterstock". No fixed structure. Empty or null removes a line. At most 500 files per call, 1000 characters per line; one url that is no file of the Library refuses the whole call. Credits are no content: nothing to publish, no change in the experience's log.

plan_asset_names reads

Step 1 of naming the Library's files by their use (#298) – read-only.

plan_asset_names { experience }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

the names every used file would take, by its first use in the scenes' order: an entry's printed image p118-1_target.webp, its colour picture p118-1_image.webp, another file of the entry or its own entity p118-1_<asset id>.glb, a surface's reference image <scene>_<surface>.webp, a shared entity's file <entity>_<asset id>.ext, the environment's environment_world / environment_sky. A file used in several places takes the first (more counts the rest); unused files and files only a plugin's source names keep their names; two files that would take one name get -2, -3. renames = only the files whose name changes: { url, imported, from, to, use: { kind, ref, scene }, more }. The name only – every URL stays, so no use breaks; an imported file (read-only) gets a listed name. Show the list to the person, then apply_asset_names.

apply_asset_names writes

Step 2 of naming the Library's files by their use (#298).

apply_asset_names { experience }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

makes the plan again (plan_asset_names – it may have changed since) and renames those files in one step – only after the person saw the plan. The name only: every URL and every use stays; an imported file's listed name is kept by its URL. Names are no content: nothing to publish, no change in the experience's log.

Plugins

list_plugins reads

The experience's plugin sources (the Code tab, the Library's scripts).

list_plugins { experience }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

id, size, usages (the draft's rows that use a type it registers), who saved it, when – without the source (get_plugin).

get_plugin reads

One plugin source with the component, layer, node and pass types it registers (read from the text).

get_plugin { experience, plugin }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
pluginstringthe plugin's id, e.g. tint

put_plugin writes

Saves a plugin source (new or changed; at most 256 KB; a change is recorded).

put_plugin { experience, plugin, source }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
pluginstringthe plugin's id, e.g. tint
sourcestringthe TypeScript source
Details

TypeScript that exports register(api) – see osct://guides/plugins: api.registerLayer(type, spec, { glsl }) for a material layer, api.registerComponent(type, spec, apply) for code on a node, api.registerNodeType(type, spec, build) for a node type of its own, api.three for three.js (never import it), api.loadText(url) for a shader file of the Library (upload_asset, kind shader – in a material's or pass's build, never a layer's glsl), api.feedback({ width, height, fragment }) for a GPU feedback buffer and api.shadertoy(source) for a Shadertoy pass as its fragment (plugin API 1.6). Nothing runs here: the person presses Run in the Code tab to see it on the stage; readers get the saved source with the person's next Publish in the editor (transpiled, not type-checked).

upload_plugin writes

Uploads a script file from this computer (.ts or .js, at most 256 KB, UTF-8 text) as a plugin source – what the editor's Library does with a dropped script.

upload_plugin { experience, file, plugin?, replace? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
filestringa local file path (.ts or .js)
plugin optionalstringthe plugin's id (default: from the file's name)
replace optionalbooleantrue: the file replaces the source of an existing plugin
Details

The id is plugin or the file's name (Wobble Effect.ts → wobble-effect); an id that exists is refused (409 plugin-exists) unless replace: true, which makes the file that plugin's new source. A change is recorded. Answers the plugin and the types it registers (read from its text).

plugin_usages reads

Where the draft uses what a plugin source registers – the experience's passes, scenes, targets, shared entities and entries that name one of its types – and those types.

plugin_usages { experience, plugin }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
pluginstringthe plugin's id, e.g. tint

delete_plugin replaces or removes

Removes a plugin source from the Code tab.

delete_plugin { experience, plugin, force? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
pluginstringthe plugin's id, e.g. tint
force optionalboolean
Details

Refused while the draft uses a type it registers (409 plugin-in-use with the usages) unless force.

New experiences, import and deliveries

create_experience writes

Makes a new, empty experience (#343).

create_experience { slug, title }
ParameterTypeWhat
slugstringthe experience's id and reader path /<slug>/: lower-case a–z, 0–9 and -, at most 64
titlestringthe experience's title (can be changed later: update_experience)
Details

a draft with one scene (a double page) and nothing on it. slug is its id – its address in the reader (https://<instance>/<slug>/) and its content store's folder: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, none of the site's own paths (editor, api, docs, scene, entry, …; 400 reserved-slug), not an experience's id already (409 duplicate-id). Ask the person for the slug – it can't be changed once the experience is published (printed QR codes and shared links depend on it). To bring in an existing configuration instead: import_experience.

preview_import reads

What an import would bring in, before anything is imported – read-only, takes import_experience's sources.

preview_import { url?, configuration?, assetsBase?, source?, experience? }
ParameterTypeWhat
url optionalstringa game.config.json to fetch
configuration optionalobjectthe game configuration itself
assetsBase optionalstringthe origin the configuration's /assets/content/… paths resolve against – its files.json is read from there, so the Library lists the imported files (a base without one imports with none)
source optional"cdn""cdn" = an experience's current version on the instance's CDN (CONTENT_BASE_URL/<experience>)
experience optionalstringwith source cdn: whose store to read – default the instance's own experience (400 invalid-experience when it has none)
Details

source: "cdn" (the current version of an experience on the instance's CDN – experience, default the instance's own), url (a game.config.json to fetch) or configuration. Answers the content base and its latest.json (build, when it became current), incoming (the one experience's id and title, the build, its date, app and schema version), counts (scenes, entries, targets, shared entities) and existing – the draft of that id the import would replace (what it is based on, its edits since, where it is live), null for a new experience. Tell the person which experience and build comes in and, when existing, that its draft is replaced and its edits lost; then import_experience with experience = incoming.experience and the same source.

import_experience replaces or removes

Replaces an experience's content rows from a game configuration (the content build's game.config.json, content schema 3.x – another is refused, 400 invalid-configuration).

import_experience { experience, url?, configuration?, assetsBase?, source?, confirm? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe configuration's own experience.id (preview_import's incoming.experience) – another id is refused (400 invalid-configuration)
url optionalstringa game.config.json to fetch
configuration optionalobjectthe game configuration itself
assetsBase optionalstringthe origin the configuration's /assets/content/… paths resolve against – its files.json is read from there, so the Library lists the imported files (a base without one imports with none)
source optional"cdn""cdn" = the current version of experience on the instance's CDN (CONTENT_BASE_URL/<experience>)
confirm optionalstringthe second step: the confirmation id of the comparison the person agreed to
Details

url fetches it (e.g. the reader's dev server http://localhost:5174/src/game.config.json), or pass configuration; source: "cdn" imports the current version of this experience on the instance's CDN (its own store there). assetsBase = where its /assets/content/… paths resolve. The change and publish logs stay; edits made since are replaced. **Two steps when the experience exists**: the first call imports nothing and answers comparison – the incoming build (id, date, app and schema version) against what the draft is based on and its edits since that import – and a short-lived confirmation. Show the comparison to the person and ask; only with their yes call again with the same arguments and confirm: <confirmation.id>. A new experience is imported at once. To tell the person first which experience and build would come in (the CDN's experience id among it), call preview_import.

preview_delivery reads

What a publisher's delivery would do to the experience's draft – read-only, nothing is written.

preview_delivery { experience, plan?, file?, overwrite? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
plan optional{ name, source, scenes, entries }the delivery plan (shared/api/deliveries.ts DeliveryPlan): name, source?, scenes?, entries – files are Library files by the asset's id or URL, uploaded before
file optionalstringinstead of plan: the path of a JSON delivery plan on this computer (as the CLI writes it); its own apply / overwrite are ignored
overwrite optionalbooleanwrite the conflicts too – only when the person asked for it
Details

Takes the delivery plan (inline plan or a JSON file): the scenes its entries need, the entries with their targets, the Library files they name by the asset's id or URL (upload them first with upload_asset; this tool never uploads or converts). Answers summary – the comparison for the person: per scene, entry and target new / changed (the fields: image, imageSrc, video) / same / conflict (edited in the editor since the last delivery – left as it is unless overwrite), the problems that stop it (an unknown scene or file, a target id in use, more than 10 targets on a scene) and the warnings – with counts, the items that are not same and a confirmation. Show the summary to the person; only with their yes call import_delivery with the same plan and confirm: confirmation.id.

import_delivery replaces or removes

Writes a publisher's delivery into the experience's draft – **two steps**, as import_experience.

import_delivery { experience, plan?, file?, overwrite?, confirm? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
plan optional{ name, source, scenes, entries }the delivery plan (shared/api/deliveries.ts DeliveryPlan): name, source?, scenes?, entries – files are Library files by the asset's id or URL, uploaded before
file optionalstringinstead of plan: the path of a JSON delivery plan on this computer (as the CLI writes it); its own apply / overwrite are ignored
overwrite optionalbooleanwrite the conflicts too – only when the person asked for it
confirm optionalstringthe second step: the confirmation id of the comparison the person agreed to
Details

without confirm it writes nothing and answers the comparison (preview_delivery's summary, counts, items, problems, warnings) and a confirmation. Show the summary to the person and ask; only with their yes call again with the same experience, plan (or file), overwrite and confirm: confirmation.id. The comparison is made again then: when anything changed meanwhile (the draft, the plan) nothing is written and the new comparison comes back (void) to show again. Written in one transaction: new scenes, entries and targets; an existing entry keeps its texts, category and scene – only its picture and its target's image and video follow the delivery; conflicts stay as they are unless overwrite: true (only when the person asked). Each write is a change naming the delivery – the editor's history (revert_change) takes it back. A plan with problems is never written.

list_deliveries reads

The experience's applied deliveries, newest first.

list_deliveries { experience, limit? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
limit optionalintegerdefault 50
Details

id, name, source, counts (new / changed / same / conflict), who (user, the AI connection's token name), when, and how many changes of the log name it (list_changes shows them with delivery). A comparison leaves no row.

History

list_changes reads

The change log, newest first.

list_changes { experience, limit? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
limit optionalinteger
Details

id, kind (entity | target | entry | scene | order | groups | environment | passes | appearance | experience | plugin | asset), ref, before, after, user, when; set / reverts for a revert's changes, notRevertable = why revert_change cannot take it back (null: it can). limit default 50, at most 500.

list_versions reads

The publish log, newest first.

list_versions { experience }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
Details

env, build, hash, who, when, note.

revert_change replaces or removes

Takes one saved change back (list_changes' id).

revert_change { experience, change, apply? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
changestringThe change's id (list_changes)
apply optionalboolean
Details

its before is written again as a NEW change, so nothing is erased and the revert can itself be reverted. Later changes of the same thing (the same entity, target, entry, scene; the same fields of the experience) would be lost, so they are reverted with it, newest first (plan.later). A thing that no longer holds what a change wrote is a conflict – listed, never overwritten. Creations, removals, moved entries, plugin sources and deleted files are not revertable. **Two steps**: without apply the plan; show it to the person, with their yes call again with apply: true. The draft only – readers see it with the next publish.

revert_to replaces or removes

Goes back to the state right after one saved change (list_changes' id).

revert_to { experience, after, apply? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
afterstringThe change to go back to (list_changes' id) – it stays, everything after it is reverted
apply optionalboolean
Details

every change saved after it – by anyone – is reverted, newest first, as one new change set. Conflicts are listed and left alone, kinds the log cannot take back are listed as not revertable. **Two steps**: without apply the plan (the changes, plan.others = other people whose changes go); show it to the person, with their yes call again with apply: true. The draft only – never a publish.

Seeing and publishing

render_scene reads

A picture (PNG) of one scene of the experience's DRAFT as the editor's stage shows it – the desk, the surfaces with their reference images, the printed images and the entities as the reader sees them – to check a placement yourself after a

render_scene { experience, scene, view, width, height }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
scenestringthe scene's id (get_experience, list_scenes)
view"reader" | "top" | "low" | "far"
widthintegerthe picture's width in px
heightintegerthe picture's height in px
Details

save instead of asking the person. view: the stage's camera presets – reader (default: 35 cm above, tilted 30°, as a reader holds the phone), top (straight down), low (from the side, 75°), far (70 cm away, the whole scene). Runs the computer's own Chrome or Edge headless (OSCT_BROWSER names another) and takes 5–30 s; the PNG is also saved, its path in file. Shows what the editor shows: the live stage at the moment of the picture (an animation's frame), the floor grid and the axis as the editor's defaults draw them.

publish writes

Writes the draft as a content version into the content store of this instance's own environment – an instance publishes there and nowhere else (a local development API.

publish { experience, env?, note? }
ParameterTypeWhat
experiencestringthe experience's id (list_experiences)
env optionalstringthe instance's own environment (default)
note optionalstring
Details

local, the staging API: staging; any other env → 403 other-environment). env may be left out: the instance's own. The answer's store says where it went: cdn (the CDN has priority where one is connected) or server (this API's own store, with warning: no edge caching – tell the person). **production is refused** – publishing to readers is the person's Publish button in the editor. Signed in with an AI connection's token (osct_…) the API refuses every environment (403 not-for-ai): then the person publishes in the editor. 409 unknown-components, unknown-node-types or unknown-materials when a node uses a component, a node type or a material no compiled plugin provides, unknown-passes when the experience's or a scene's post-processing names a pass no compiled plugin provides (the Code tab's sources reach readers through the content build only). Every experience has its own store in the environment: a publish replaces only this experience's previous build there. The other refusals: 400 invalid-env, invalid-note; 404 not-found (no such experience); 502 content-store-failed and 500 content-store-unconfigured (the store could not be read or written – nothing went live). Every refusal comes with a hint.
